root_idea.summary: The root centers on holding, gathering, or containing something so that it is not released, especially breath or emotion.
root_idea.development: This principle extends from containing wrath, grief, or breath to silence, withholding a camel's cud, closing a filled waterskin, retaining water in conduits, and joining or fastening parts.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized adjective كَظِيم.
Displayed under the singular active-participle citation form كَاظِم; the supplied Quran form is its plural.
Displayed under the passive-participle citation form مَكْظُوم.

senses.definition: Inwardly grief-laden, with emotion or grief held in rather than openly expressed.
senses.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of a person experiencing intense inward sorrow or distress; the sense combines containment of emotion with its resulting grief-stricken state.

senses.definition: One who restrains or suppresses intense emotion, especially anger.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural form كَاظِمِينَ is used for people holding anger or anguish in; the construction does not require that the emotion be outwardly displayed.

senses.definition: Constrained by emotion or breath held in; inwardly stifled and distressed.
senses.usage_conditions: A passive state in which grief or anguish is contained within, rather than released; attested in the Quranic description of the anguished speaker.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Holding one's breath; by extension, remaining silent or refraining from speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The silence sense is an expressive extension of breath being held in.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to cease regurgitating or ruminating its cud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage concerning the camel's retention or cessation of its cud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To close or tie a filled waterskin, preventing what it contains from escaping.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction applied to a waterskin after it has been filled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The outlet or passage through which breath exits.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is used in expressions referring to seizing or obstructing a person's breath passage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Subterranean conduits or excavated channels carrying water from one well to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural of كِظَامَة in this technical water-management usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ring joining the threads at the end of an iron balance beam.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical fastening term for the part that gathers and holds the balance threads together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strap attached to the string of an Arab bow and looped around the upper end of its bow limb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical bow-making term for a connecting or retaining strap.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Repressing or restraining wrath is represented by the Quranic active-participle sense.
Self-restraint is covered by the broader sense of holding intense emotion in.
An illustrative idiom followed only by a cross-reference, without an independent definition in the supplied unit.
Restraining one's wrath is the same lexical branch as the represented Quranic sense.
The technical meaning of subterranean water conduits is represented separately.

cautions: كَظِيم and مَكْظُوم combine the idea of inward containment with its emotional result, so translations may alternate between suppressing emotion, being grief-laden, and being distressed.
The Quranic form كَاظِمِينَ is presented under the singular dictionary citation form كَاظِم.
